# Every build, against real Safari

We do not ask you to take our word for it. Every change to Lumen is built on a Mac with real Safari: a profile is compared with it, every request around the proxy is looked for, and the results are recorded. Here is what is measured, how, and the numbers of the latest runs — including what differs.

## A profile against Safari on the same Mac

Safari and a profile open the same pages on one Mac: Safari driven by safaridriver, the profile in a window of its own of the same size. Every value a page or a server can measure is compared.

What is compared

Identical

Details

The probe page

everything a page can measure about the engine and the Mac

434 of 448

every must-match key

Navigator and screen, language and Intl, time zone, canvas — the same data URL byte for byte, WebGL — vendor, renderer, extensions and parameters, font metrics. The 14 differences are below, with their reasons.

Request headers

navigation, fetch and XHR

31 of 31

set and order

The same headers in the same order as Safari’s.

TLS and HTTP/2

tls.peet.ws

15 of 15

identical

ClientHello — JA3, JA4, ciphers and extensions apart from random GREASE; HTTP/2 SETTINGS, WINDOW_UPDATE and pseudo-header order; TCP SYN.

In the run of build ce64ca1 the measuring service did not answer Safari, so nothing was compared; the previous run is shown.

Window geometry

with one tab and with two

10 of 10

and with two tabs

Outer and inner window size, screen position, visualViewport. 52 px of toolbar with one tab and 90 px with two, as in Safari 26.

Permissions and APIs

permission states, storage quota, speech voices

16 of 17

one difference

Before permission, Safari lists a camera and a microphone, a profile only the microphone: macOS hides the camera from an app not yet allowed to use it. Allow Lumen the camera once and the lists match.

## What differs — and why

Of the probe’s 448 signals, 14 differ. We show all of them. Eight come from the test bench, not the product; six are real differences from Safari, and none of them is a must-match key.

| Signals | Count | Where | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Apple Pay and Web Push`ApplePaySession`, `ApplePaySetup`, `MerchantValidationEvent`, `PaymentRequest`, `PushManager` | 5 | in the product | Safari’s alone: WebKit enables them only for an app with Safari’s entitlements. Exposing objects that cannot work would be worse. |
| Number of window’s own properties`windowOwnCount` | 1 | in the product | Follows from the row above: Safari has the Apple Pay and Web Push objects, and a default profile has no WebRTC either. |
| Language`language`, `languages`, the `Intl` locale, the date string | 4 | on the bench | The self-test gives the profile German on purpose, to check that it reaches the page. |
| Window size`innerSize`, `outerSize` | 2 | on the bench | The self-test’s probe runs in a hidden window. Real window sizes are compared separately — the geometry above, 10 of 10. |
| webdriver and the error stack`navigator.webdriver`, stack depth | 2 | on the bench | Safari under safaridriver reports `webdriver = true`; the stack differs because of how the bench runs the script. |

## Leak checks

Separate checks run a profile behind real proxies on the CI machine and look for any way around them. A check fails at the first request that goes around.

QUIC and HTTP/3

stays on the proxy

Without a proxy, cloudflare-quic.com answers a profile over HTTP/3; through an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy, over HTTP/2, and the proxy sees every request. UDP is never even asked of the proxy.

leak_check · every build

WebRTC

off in a proxied profile

No `RTCPeerConnection` in the page, its frames or its workers. A control without a proxy does get its public address over STUN — so the check sees a leak when there is one.

leak_check and the self-test

DNS

never around the proxy

The test page asks for names to be resolved early: dns-prefetch, preconnect, a Link header. The packet capture holds no DNS question for any of them.

egress_check

Requests to the computer itself

refused

A page, a frame and a worker reach for `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1` and `0.0.0.0`. Each request is refused; a loopback listener takes no connection.

self-test

Certificates

refused at the handshake

A test server presents a certificate the system would go to the network to complete. In a proxied profile it is refused at the handshake — through the proxy.

self-test

Every packet off the machine

none around the proxy

While a profile opens a page that makes every kind of request, CI records every packet leaving the machine with the process that sent it: 2,410 packets in the latest run.

egress_check · pktap

Writes to disk

nothing in Safari’s folders

Every write of the app and WebKit is traced: a profile writes nothing where the real Safari keeps its data. In the latest run, a trace of 606,017 lines.

disk_check · fs_usage

Safari’s services

never called

Search suggestions, Safe Browsing, translation, Apple Pay and the other services that go to the network from processes of their own are not called from a profile’s process: connections to them are refused.

self-test and packet capture

## What every build checks

These steps run on every change to the code. If any required one fails, the build is red.

| Step | What it checks | Latest run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core unit tests | Encryption, the vault, sync, cookie import, warm-up — on Linux and on macOS | 223 tests on macOS, 0 failures |
| Scripts in two engines | The scripts a profile adds to a page behave like built-in functions — in V8 and in JavaScriptCore, Safari’s engine | passed |
| Self-test on real WebKit | Profile isolation, the proxy and fail-closed, sealing on stop, passwords, cookies, sync between two Macs, warm-up, Safari’s window in a profile’s process | 274 checks, 0 failures |
| Safari’s classes | That Safari’s interface in a profile finds everything it relies on: if a macOS update removes something, the build shows it | passed |
| Compared with Safari | The probe, headers, TLS and HTTP/2, window geometry, APIs | 434 of 448; 0 must-match differences |
| Leaks | QUIC, WebRTC, DNS, requests to the computer itself | passed |
| Packets and disk | Every packet off the machine and every write to disk around the self-test | no packet around the proxy |
| Logs | Nothing of yours reaches the system log in the clear | passed |
| Languages | The Russian and English interfaces hold the same strings | passed |

## Check it yourself

All you need is your Mac and any proxy.

1. The address In a profile with a proxy, open a page that shows your IP address. It must be the proxy’s.
2. Fail-closed Switch the proxy off and reload. The page must not open — let alone show your real address.
3. The fingerprint Open the same fingerprint test page in Safari and in a profile on this Mac. The values match — apart from Apple Pay and Web Push.

If the test page says “Canvas: Spoofed”, open it in plain Safari 26: deviceinfo.me says the same there. Its test knows only an older PNG length, and today’s WebKit encodes the same picture differently.
